nodes.prompt:
REPO: /Users/aleph/Projects/telegram-mcp-go. The Python->Go port is code-complete: internal/config, internal/session, internal/kit(+paths), internal/mcpserver, nine tool packages (132 tools), cmd/telegram-mcp-go with gen-session/migrate-session. Python sources are staged for deletion; do not touch git state (NEVER git add/commit).
Go 1.27.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin/go. No new go.mod dependencies. Offline tests only (no network, no real Telegram). gofmt + go vet clean. Never edit files outside your SCOPE. Report DELIVERABLE + VERIFY output verbatim.

PROBLEM: the binary does not serve MCP yet. Every tool package registers its tools via init() into mcpserver.DefaultRegistry (internal/mcpserver/tool.go:68), but cmd/telegram-mcp-go/main.go never blank-imports them and never installs the modules' runtime seams, so a running binary serves 0 tools. mcpserver.Main (internal/mcpserver/main.go:22) already parses --dry-run, loads config, builds from DefaultRegistry and serves; it is never called.

TASK: write the boot wiring.
1. New package internal/boot: blank-import all nine tool packages (accounts, chats, contacts, events, folders, groups, media, messages, profile) and provide an Install(src config.EnvSource) error (name is yours) that loads config once and installs every module's runtime seam with lazy, session-backed clients using internal/session.Connect (internal/session/connect.go:66; ConnectOptions: Label, Identity, NewClient func() (ClientHandle, error), ExpectedUsername, Shared, lock options). Single-account mode first; refuse/clarify multi-account instead of guessing; document deferrals.
   Seams to satisfy (read each module's file for exact field sets):
   - messages.Configure(messages.Runtime{...}) (messages.go:53); adapter exists: messages.NewGogramClient(*telegram.Client) (client.go:102).
   - groups.SetRuntime(groups.Runtime{...}) (groups.go:98); groups.Client is satisfied directly by *telegram.Client (assertion groups.go:71).
   - chats.SetClientProvider(chats.ClientProvider) (chats.go:307/322); chats has NO gogram adapter — write one inside internal/boot implementing chats.Client (chats.go:226) over *telegram.Client.
   - contacts.Configure(*contacts.Deps) (contacts.go:177); events.Configure(events.Deps) (events/deps.go:110) — check how events' Register (events.go:48) is invoked and keep the 132-tool surface unchanged.
   - folders.Deps (folders.go:31, Client :130), media.Deps (media.go:52, Client :91), profile.Deps + Client (profile.go:37/:180), accounts (init registers list_accounts; wire whatever it needs, it may need nothing client-side).
   For every module whose Client interface lacks a gogram adapter, put the adapter in internal/boot (do NOT add gogram imports under internal/tools/**, that is a recorded gate).
2. Wire cmd/telegram-mcp-go/main.go: default invocation (no subcommand, and any flag like --dry-run) must install the boot wiring and call mcpserver.Main(args, stdout, stderr). Keep gen-session, migrate-session, help semantics unchanged. Update/extend cmd tests.
3. PROVE end-to-end (verbatim output):
   a. go build ./... ; go vet ./... ; go test ./... -count=1  (all exit 0)
   b. WITH DUMMY ENV (mirror internal/config tests; set TELEGRAM_API_ID/HASH and whatever session var config.Load needs, e.g. TELEGRAM_SESSION_STRING): `go run ./cmd/telegram-mcp-go --dry-run` prints a JSON array; its length is 132 and the name set equals .omo/go-port/parity/inventory.json names. Capture the count line and the exact command. It must not touch the network nor a real session.
   c. Add a regression test (cmd or boot) that exercises the no-args dry-run path in-process with dummy env and asserts 132 — keep it.
SCOPE: internal/boot/** (new) and cmd/telegram-mcp-go/** only. Do NOT edit internal/tools/**, internal/mcpserver/**, internal/session/**, internal/kit/**, go.mod/go.sum, .omo/**. If a seam genuinely cannot be satisfied without editing those, STOP and report FAIL with the exact blocker instead.
STOP WHEN: dry-run from the real cmd prints exactly 132 tools and all gates are green.
